title: Tunisia’s 2024 drinking-water salinity baseline spans 1.5–3 g/L from north to south

rootCauses.cause: The cited sources document a southern source-water quality constraint, but do not establish its underlying cause (SRC-TG-604).
SONEDE reported deploying desalination and blending as responses to drinking-water quality concerns; these are responses rather than causes of salinity (SRC-TG-603, SRC-TG-604).

dataGaps: The 2001 report presents the southern drinking-water salinity change without giving the measurement years or method; it is historical evidence, not a current quality estimate.
The 2017 groundwater salinity table has no stated measurement year or method and reports raw resource classes, not salinity at household taps.

A claim that 85% of groundwater exceeds 1.5 g/L is not supported by these cited figures: SONEDE's table reports 79.9% above 1.5 g/L nationally (2017 presentation, no reference year), while its southern share is 99.7%.
No primary DGRE series, governorate-specific tap-water sampling, or independently checked recent salinity time series was located.
The 2001 report discusses phosphogypsum disposal nationally and Gabès impacts, but does not verify a 2017 decision to stop Gabès discharges; that specific claim remains unsubstantiated.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content:
Tunisia’s national climate contribution gives a 2024 drinking-water baseline of 1.5–3 g/L across the north and south (SRC-TG-605). It does not assign a mean or a sampling distribution to any governorate.

Salinity constrained water quality in southern Tunisia during the historical periods documented by the sources. The 2001 national environment report states that average drinking-water salinity in the South improved from 2.4 to 1.4 g/L, but gives no measurement years or method (SRC-TG-603). A SONEDE official's 2017 presentation classifies only 3 Mm3 of 859 Mm3 of southern groundwater resources as below 1.5 g/L salinity, though the data year is unspecified (SRC-TG-604). That resource estimate does not establish the quality of water delivered to households, which can be affected by treatment and blending; no current estimate is supported here.

sections.heading: Root causes
sections.content: The available evidence documents saline source water as a constraint: the SONEDE presentation's salinity table shows almost all southern groundwater above 1.5 g/L, although its data year and method are unspecified (SRC-TG-604). The 2001 environment report says new northern reservoirs and southern groundwater desalination, combined with a water-mixing programme, improved drinking-water quality (SRC-TG-603). The evidence does not isolate the contribution of each intervention or establish a current causal trend.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.content: The 2001 report gives southern average drinking-water salinity as 2.4 then 1.4 g/L, without dating the two measurements (SRC-TG-603). In a 2017 presentation, SONEDE reports 3 Mm3 below 1.5 g/L out of 859 Mm3 of southern groundwater resources; nationally, its table gives 381 Mm3 out of 1,898 Mm3 below that threshold (SRC-TG-604). The 2001 report also states phosphogypsum disposal at 13,000 tonnes/day nationally and mentions Gabès among affected industrial regions, but this does not substantiate a 2017 stop order for Gabès discharges (SRC-TG-603).

sections.heading: Why confidence is what it is
sections.content: Confidence is medium for the existence of a historical salinity constraint because the report and SONEDE presentation are official sources and the figures are explicit. Confidence is limited for present-day exposure: the older drinking-water figures lack dates and methods, and the later salinity table concerns groundwater resources, with no stated reference year, rather than delivered water. The specific allegation of a 2017 Gabès discharge stoppage is not evidenced here.

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content: Water desalination links saline source quality to energy demand; the cited sources describe desalination programmes but do not quantify associated energy use (SRC-TG-603, SRC-TG-604).

sections.heading: Leads for phase 2
sections.content: - SONEDE's regional programme to improve drinking-water quality through desalination and water mixing (SRC-TG-603, SRC-TG-604).

sections.heading: Verification
sections.content:
The dated drinking-water baseline is distinct from the earlier groundwater resource inventory. Historical water-quality observations without sampling dates remain narrative evidence; the 2035 target is prospective (SRC-TG-605, SRC-TG-603, SRC-TG-604).

**Independent review, 21 November 2026:** pass. Checked against the originals: CDN 3.0 Tableau 11, p. 57 (SRC-TG-605), 2024 drinking-water salinity 1.5-3 g/L and 2035 target; RNE 2001 water-resources section (SRC-TG-603); SONEDE desalination workshop slides, 25 May 2017, salinity table (SRC-TG-604). No corrections. Independent teammate sign-off is outstanding; reviewer and author share the TahaGHZ identity, so the record is not validated.

resolvedSources.title: Rapport national sur l'état de l'environnement 2001
resolvedSources.publisher: Ministère de l'Environnement et de l'Aménagement du Territoire (MEAT), Tunisie
resolvedSources.extracts:
"L'état des ressources naturelles", salinity indicator (IS), printed pp. 19-20:

> 0 - 1,5 g/l : Cette plage de salinité des eaux correspond aux eaux de bonne qualité utilisables comme eaux potables et eaux d'irrigation pour toutes les cultures.

> 1,5 - 3 g/l : Cette plage concerne l'eau d'irrigation valable pour la plupart des cultures et celle réservée à l'industrie.

Table "Salinité : Indicateur (IS)" (volumes in Mm3; source line under the table: "Stratégie du secteur de l'eau en Tunisie à long terme (2030) - Eau XXI, 1998"):

> Eaux de surface 1955 72 | 745 28 | - -
> Eaux des nappes phréatiques 57,5 8 | 510,5 71 | 151 21
> Eaux des nappes profondes 250 20 | 1000 80 | - -
> Total 2 262,5 48,5 | 2255,5 48,3 | 151 3,2

(columns: 0-1,5 g/l volume and %; 1,5-5 g/l volume and %; > 5 g/l volume and %)

> Si on déduit la quantité d'eau de bonne qualité (Rs < 1,5 g) réservée à l'eau potable, seulement 37,3 % des ressources en eau peuvent être utilisées en irrigation sans risque de salinisation.

English gloss: The report classes water below 1.5 g/L as good for drinking and all crops. Citing the Eau XXI strategy (1998), it puts 8% of shallow-aquifer and 20% of deep-aquifer resources below 1.5 g/L (57.5 of 719 Mm3 and 250 of 1,250 Mm3), against 72% of surface water.

Industrial pollution, printed p. 140:

> le phosphogypse : 13 000 t/jour qui sont soit stockées à l'air libre, soit rejetés dans la mer ;

English gloss: Phosphogypsum: 13,000 t/day, either stored in the open or discharged into the sea (national figure for industrial solid waste).

Printed p. 139:

> [...] la région du Golfe de Gabès, où les complexes chimiques sont responsables à la création de plusieurs sources de nuisances (rejets de phosphogypse et divers produits polluants).
resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl + pdftotext (layout), Latin-1 converted; saw: full text. Two-column layout; sentences were re-joined across columns, wording unchanged.
- The salinity table is a 1998 strategy estimate repeated in 2002, not a new measurement.
- The 13,000 t/day figure is stated nationally (Gabès and Sfax plants are both mentioned elsewhere); it is not attributed to Gabès alone in this report.

resolvedSources.title: La contribution du dessalement dans la mobilisation des ressources en eau en Tunisie (presentation, IRESA-GIZ workshop, Gammarth, 25 May 2017)
resolvedSources.publisher: SONEDE (Fethi Kamel, Directeur central conseiller à la DG); hosted by energypedia
resolvedSources.extracts:
Slide 7, "Ressources en eau selon la salinité" (pdftotext -raw):

> La répartition géographique en Mm3 des ressources en eau souterraine en Tunisie selon la salinité est la suivante:
> Région (Mm3) | Salinité < 1.5 g/l | Salinité 1.5 ­ 3 g/l | Salinité 3 ­ 5 g/l | Salinité > 5 g/l | Total
> Nord 211 205 119 23 558
> Centre 167 191 88 35 481
> Sud 3 500 281 75 859
> Total 381 896 488 133 1898
> Pourcentage 20.1% 47.2% 25.7% 7% 100%

English gloss: Of 1,898 Mm3 of groundwater, 381 Mm3 (20.1%) is below 1.5 g/L; in the South only 3 of 859 Mm3 is. No reference year is given.

Slide 22, "Programme d'amélioration de la qualité d'eau":

> la première phase concerne les régions ayant plus que 2 g/l de salinité et une population supérieure à 4000 habitants. · Mise en service en 2016 et début 2017

> La deuxième phase porte sur les régions ayant entre 1.5 g/l et 2.0 g/l de salinité et une population supérieure à 4000 habitants. ·Etude achevée, encours de préparation des appels d'offres et démarrage de certains travaux (forages).

Slide 23, "Projets de la première phase (Mai 2017)": ten brackish-water reverse-osmosis plants totalling 36,200 m3/day at Tozeur, Nafta, Hezoua (Tozeur), Kébili, Souk Lahad, Douz (Kébili), Matmata, Mareth (Gabès), Béni Khédache (Médenine) and Belkhir (Gafsa, EDR), with progress 98-100%.

Slide 19 (existing SONEDE brackish plants), raw-water salinity:

> Salinité eau brute 3,2 g/l 6 g/l 6 g/l 3.7 g/l 14g/l

(for Gabès, Djerba, Zarzis, Kerkennah, Bengardène respectively)

- Opened via: curl + pdftotext (layout and raw); saw: full slide deck.
- Conference slides by a SONEDE senior official; tier B. The groundwater salinity table has no stated data year or method. The distributed-water salinity map on slide 22 is an image; its class legend (<0.5 to >2.0 g/L) was readable, its areas were not.

resolvedSources.title: Contribution déterminée au niveau national 3.0, tableau 11
resolvedSources.extracts:
Tableau 11, water-quality baseline for 2024:

> Salinité d’eau potable 1,5-3 g/l (entre Nord et Sud)

It gives a national north–south range, without local sampling dates or regional averages. The 2035 target is at or below 1.5 g/L. The same table reports 31 tertiary wastewater plants out of 127 for 2024.
